chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn Mahzīyār narrated from his brother, ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, who said:

I wrote to him asking about an owned slave when death approaches him, and his master frees him at that hour, so he departs from the world as a free man. Is there for the master a reward in freeing him then, or is it better that he leave him as an owned slave, such that he would have reward if he dies while still owned by him?

So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "The slave is to be left as owned in the state of his death, for that is more rewarding for his master. And this emancipation at that hour was not beneficial for him."

key_terms.مَمْلُوكًا: remaining in a state of ownership

ai.seo_question: Is freeing a slave at the moment of death more rewarding than leaving him as owned?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the emancipation of a slave at the moment of death. It states that leaving the slave in his owned status at that final hour is more rewarding for the master, because manumission at such a time does not benefit the dying slave.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3559 - Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar narrated from his brother, Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
I wrote to Imam (as) asking about a slave who is near death, and his master frees him at that moment so that he leaves this world as a free man. Does the master earn a reward for freeing him, or is it better to leave him as a slave so that the master gains a greater reward if he dies while still owned?
Imam (as) wrote: "It is better for the master to leave the slave as a servant at the time of his death, for this brings more reward to the master. Freeing him in such an hour offers no benefit."
